item.title: Parking in Frankston Melbourne 2026: Where to Park, What It Costs
item.description:
Parking in Frankston: The Real Guide

Driving to Frankston? You need to know where to park before you circle the block four times and end up in a loading zone. This guide covers free parking, metered spots, off-street options, permit zones, and the streets where rangers patrol most. Updated for 2026.

Free Parking in Frankston

Free parking exists in Frankston, but you need to know where:

  • Residential side streets free — best bets for free unrestricted parking, especially outside peak
  • Sundays: Most metered spots revert to free on Sundays and public holidays. Always check the sign — some zones are now 7-day
  • After hours: Many metered spots on main shopping strip become free after 6pm or 7:30pm depending on the zone

The rule in Frankston: park two or three streets back from main shopping strip and walk. Less competition, often free, and you avoid the ranger hotspots.

item.title: Schools in Frankston Melbourne 2026: State, Private and School Zones
item.description:
Schools in Frankston: What Families Need to Know

Moving to Frankston with school-age children? Schools are the second thing you research after rent. In Melbourne, school zones drive real estate decisions as much as train lines and cafe strips. Understanding Frankston’s school landscape before you sign a lease saves you from the most common mistake: assuming access to a school your address does not zone you into.

State Primary Schools

Frankston is served by government primary schools within its zone boundaries. Enrolment is based on your residential address falling within the school’s designated neighbourhood boundary. You have a right to enrol at your designated neighbourhood school.
